title: Comparison morphism from the inverse image to the derived pullback along an isomorphism
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with small pro-etale sites $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], inverse image $g^{-1}$ and structure maps $c^g_A:g^{-1}A_Y\to A_X$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E\}$ and, for $W\in\{X,Y\}$, let $\Lambda_W$ be the constant sheaf $(A_{E,n})_W$ for $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ and the completed sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}=\varprojlim_m(A_{E,m})_W$ with projections $\pi_m$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] for $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$; $D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ is the derived category of $\Lambda_W$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

*Structure isomorphism.* Put $c_\Lambda=c^g_{A_{E,n}}$ for $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$. For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ let $c_{\mathcal O_E}:g^{-1}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ be the morphism of sheaves of rings whose $m$-th component is $c^g_{A_{E,m}}\circ g^{-1}(\pi_m)$ (these are compatible with the reductions $(A_{E,m+1})_X\to(A_{E,m})_X$ by [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] (3), so they define a map into the limit); thus $\pi_m\circ c_{\mathcal O_E}=c^g_{A_{E,m}}\circ g^{-1}(\pi_m)$ for every $m$. By [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] (2) and (3), $c_\Lambda$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings (for $\mathcal O_E$ it is the composite of the canonical isomorphism $g^{-1}\varprojlim_m(A_{E,m})_Y\to\varprojlim_mg^{-1}(A_{E,m})_Y$ with $\varprojlim_mc^g_{A_{E,m}}$). For a complex $M$ of $\Lambda_Y$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the termwise inverse image $g^{-1}M$ is a complex of $g^{-1}\Lambda_Y$-modules, and it is regarded as a complex of $\Lambda_X$-modules by letting a local section $a$ of $\Lambda_X$ act as $c_\Lambda^{-1}(a)$. The underlying abelian-sheaf functor is exact by [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] (2). Kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafifications of sectionwise cokernels in the module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so transporting the action through $c_\Lambda$ leaves their underlying abelian sheaves unchanged. Thus this module functor is exact also for the completed coefficient sheaf. In particular $H^i(g^{-1}M)\cong g^{-1}H^i(M)$, as follows by preserving the kernel of $d^i$ and the image of $d^{i-1}$ and their quotient; it therefore sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms. Applying it termwise and using the localization defining the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] defines a functor $g^{-1}:D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)\to D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$.

The *comparison morphism* is the morphism
$$
 \kappa_K:g^{-1}K\longrightarrow Lg^*K
$$
in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$, for $K$ a complex of $\Lambda_Y$-modules, where at finite level $Lg^*$ is the derived module pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and at integral level it is the ambient completed pullback of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] (whose restriction is the integral operation of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]), defined as follows.

(a) *Finite level*, $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$. Here $Lg^*K=L(g_n)^*K$ is represented by the termwise module inverse image $g^*K$, $g^*K^i=g^{-1}K^i\otimes_{g^{-1}A_Y}A_X$, the change of rings along $c^g_A$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $g^*$ being exact [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact, def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. $\kappa_K$ is the class of the map of complexes whose $i$-th term $g^{-1}K^i\to g^*K^i$ is the composite of the presheaf map $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ (on sections over each object $U$) with the sheafification map [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The presheaf map respects restrictions because $(x\otimes1)|_V=x|_V\otimes1$, so its composite with sheafification defines a sheaf map. It is $A_X$-linear: $c_A^{-1}(a)x\mapsto c_A^{-1}(a)x\otimes1=x\otimes c_A(c_A^{-1}(a))=a(x\otimes1)$; and it commutes with the differentials because these are $g^{-1}(d)$ and $g^{-1}(d)\otimes1$.

(b) *Integral level*, $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$. Let $q:P\to K$ be the K-flat resolution with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution] with which $Lg^*K$ is formed in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], $P_m=P\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}}(A_{E,m})_Y$ with the reductions $r_m:P\to P_m$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, and $C_m=\operatorname{Res}_mg^*(P_m)$ (restriction of scalars along $\pi_m$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], $g^*$ the module inverse image of (a) at level $m$), with transition maps $t_m:C_{m+1}\to C_m$ induced by $P_{m+1}\to P_m$. The latter sends $x\otimes\bar a$ to $x\otimes\bar a$ using $A_{E,m+1}\to A_{E,m}$; apply $g^{-1}$, the coefficient reduction $(A_{E,m+1})_X\to(A_{E,m})_X$, and the universal property of the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] to obtain $t_m$. After restriction of scalars these are maps of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$-complexes, since $\pi_m$ is $\pi_{m+1}$ followed by that reduction. Then $Lg^*K=R\varprojlim_mC_m$ is represented by the complex $\operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}_m(C_\bullet)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined], where $1-s:\prod_mC_m\to\prod_mC_m$, $(c_m)\mapsto(c_m-t_m(c_{m+1}))$, on the termwise products [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], and the cone is that of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so that $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]^i=\prod_mC_m^{i-1}\oplus\prod_mC_m^{i}$ with differential $(b,a)\mapsto(-db-(1-s)a,\ da)$. For each $m$ let $\theta_m:g^{-1}P\to C_m$ be the map of complexes whose $i$-th term is $g^{-1}(r_m):g^{-1}P^i\to g^{-1}P^i_m$ followed by the map $g^{-1}P_m^i\to g^*P_m^i$ of (a). It is $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$-linear, $g^{-1}P$ carrying the structure through $c_{\mathcal O_E}^{-1}$ and $C_m$ through $\pi_m$, because $\pi_m\circ c_{\mathcal O_E}=c^g_{A_{E,m}}\circ g^{-1}(\pi_m)$; and $t_m\circ\theta_{m+1}=\theta_m$, because the reductions satisfy $(P_{m+1}\to P_m)\circ r_{m+1}=r_m$. Hence $\theta=(\theta_m)_m:g^{-1}P\to\prod_mC_m$ satisfies $(1-s)\circ\theta=0$, and $\tilde\theta:g^{-1}P\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$, $z\mapsto(0,\theta(z))$, is a map of complexes: $d(0,\theta(z))=(-(1-s)\theta(z),d\theta(z))=(0,\theta(dz))=\tilde\theta(dz)$. The map $g^{-1}(q):g^{-1}P\to g^{-1}K$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $g^{-1}$ being exact. Put
$$
 \kappa_K=[\tilde\theta]\circ[g^{-1}(q)]^{-1}:g^{-1}K\longrightarrow R\varprojlim_mC_m=Lg^*K .
$$
(In Mathlib terms, $\tilde\theta$ is `CochainComplex.mappingCocone.lift` of $1-s$ with first component $\theta$ and zero homotopy, up to the sign convention of the cone.)

Fix the resolutions used by [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] in making this definition. Naturality in $K$, independence of that choice up to the identifications of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined], and invertibility on the bounded constructible subcategories are separate assertions; this definition specifies the displayed morphism for the chosen representatives and resolutions.
